source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Electric Cells and Circuits
points: An **electric cell** is a source of electricity with two **terminals** — **positive (+)** and **negative (−)**.
A **battery** = two or more cells joined together.
An **electric circuit** is a **closed path** for the current; current flows only when the circuit is **complete (closed)**.

sections.heading: 2. Components and Symbols
points: Main components: **cell/battery, connecting wires, switch (key), bulb**.
A **switch** completes (ON) or breaks (OFF) the circuit.
Circuits are drawn using standard **symbols** (for cell, battery, switch, bulb, wire) to make clear **circuit diagrams**.
A bulb glows only in a **closed** circuit; a **break** anywhere stops the current.

sections.heading: 3. Conductors and Insulators
points: **Conductors** allow current to pass through (metals — copper, aluminium; graphite; the human body when wet).
**Insulators** do not allow current (plastic, rubber, wood, glass, dry air).
Wires are made of a **conductor (metal)** covered with an **insulator (plastic)** for safety.

sections.heading: 4. Effects and Safety
points: Current produces a **heating effect** (bulb, heater) and a **magnetic effect** (electromagnet, compass deflection).
**Never touch electrical devices with wet hands**; do not experiment with **mains electricity** (dangerous).
A **short circuit** or overload can cause fire → **fuses/switches** protect us.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Cell has + and − terminals; battery = cells joined; current flows only in a closed circuit.
Components: cell/battery, wires, switch, bulb; drawn with standard symbols.
Conductors = metals, graphite; insulators = plastic, rubber, wood, glass.
Current effects: heating (bulb/heater) and magnetic (electromagnet).
Safety: never touch with wet hands; avoid mains electricity.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A bulb glows **only** when the circuit is **closed/complete**.
**Graphite** is a **conductor** (a non-metal that conducts); most non-metals do not.
Wires use a **conductor (metal)** inside and an **insulator (plastic)** outside.
**Wet hands/body conduct** electricity — a serious safety risk.
